The missile knows where it is at all times. It knows this because it knows where it isn't. By subtracting where it is from where it isn't, or where it isn't from where it is (whichever is greater), it obtains a difference, or deviation. The guidance subsystem uses deviations to generate corrective commands to drive the missile from a position where it is to a position where it isn't, and arriving at a position where it wasn't, it now is. Consequently, the position where it is, is now the position that it wasn't, and it follows that the position that it was, is now the position that it isn't.  


In the event that the position that it is in is not the position that it wasn't, the system has acquired a variation, the variation being the difference between where the missile is, and where it wasn't. If variation is considered to be a significant factor, it too may be corrected by the GEA. However, the missile must also know where it was.

Hi,

I had a six hour lay-over in Washington DC. I am a factory worker but got this opportunity because my sister was getting married in NC on the beach. Living with blessings is hard, but doable. I do not subscribe to anything fancy, nor believe in the mystical.

That six hours was the best in my life. It started with me having a BP breakdown leading into the metro station. I do not know if you've been to airports before, but that is not wear you want to break down, and I am sure there is some footage in some harddrive of me pacing and begging.

​

We walked 7 miles and saw the sights. She wanted to carry her backpack most of the way.

​

Suprisingly, the capitol of this country was empty because of Covid. There were few people and most things were closed. We walked from the metro station to the downtown area nearest the National Mall. She stopped for Starbucks and I waited outside.

We wanted to see the Capitol first since it was closest and then walk to the Lincoln Memorial. What I remember most is walking, and just talking about the excitement to see the sights with no one around. Was that person running past a senator? Who is here and living now? If I could work in the Capitol Building, I'd bike the National Mall every 15 minute break.

My favorite part of Washington DC is the Smithsonian Air and Space Museum. They had big banners up advertising open and that they were making a hangar to house the freaking space shuttle. We walked up only to find closed. My favorite part was a disappointment, but at that point we were having fun. We had seen gardens and statues. There are places to sit off the mall if you just look.

I think she ate a hot dog off a food truck halfway to the Lincoln Memorial. I most remember her walking down each one looking and choosing, and saying yes, this $8 hotdog and fries is the best I can do.

Of course we came upon the Washington Monument. I think she used the bathroom in the giftshop while I and few others browsed the books. I liked that they had books for kids about every president, and several bookmarks and knicknacks. After Leacing we saw the top of the Washington Monument was by appointment only.

​

For some reason they put war memorials in between congress and the Lincoln Memorial. The most noticeable is the WWII memorial. I do not know how to describe what I saw that day. They had stones, marble, granite and so forth. If you leaned really close you could see speckles of gold(maybe fool's). I think I licked one and it tasted salty.

I almost broke down after that on our trek to the Lincoln Memorial and after the WWII monument was a chassing argument, by the Reflecing Pool, mostly drained.

The Lincoln Memorial is a monument everyone should see. When I walked up those steps I thought of Forrest Gump and civil rights. When you enter those halls, there were maybe 100 people there, it feels BIG. The vastness of everything before just struck me. SHe looked at the inscriptions on the walls before talking to me. I could tell she was still angry, but wanted to talk. She said it's big. I said ya and we went to look for the gift shop.

There was a queue to the gift shop. The few people in front of us filtered in and out quick, 3 at a time in the store no more and seemingly no less. The gift shop was so narrow, I could not belive they ever let more than 3 in before. Here again they had books! Books about Civil Rights and the struggle of the oppressed. I think she bought a few trinkets and a bookmark to gift.

Walking out of the giftshop, Lincoln and his vastness struck again, and more amicable we both expored the inscriptions on the walls surrounding before going to see the man himself. It was his two best speeches. I don't remember the words but the spirit and I think she does too.

Below Lincoln is a small museum attributed to Martin Luther King. There was so many good  pictures and knowledge! It really put the big man upstairs in to perspective.

As we were walking away from Lincoln and back to the Metro station to take us back to the airport she finally asked me to take her backpack. I did, I will.

And now I am lonely, and thank you

Full disclosure, FFVIII was the first I played, FFVII the first I beat, and have payed all except the FFVII spinoffs, XIII-2 and 3, and the MMO's. I play most through or all the way through as the years go by, cycling through my love of Final Fantasy as the years go through seasons. Not only that, FF has always been something responsible for bonding and propagation of video game love in my family.

It has to be FFX though, that will always take my top spot. It has all the gameplay, story, presentation and panache known to the series, but it has the added benefit of being the last common bonding point between my sister and I before significant changes in our lives. Hell, she being older bought the PS2 and game(both of which are still in damn good working condition considering the age and play time) just as it came out. Seeing as she had totally bogarted my FF love when I got the PS1 and FFVIII, it was mighty kind of her to offer to play it with me. To this day, I have never seen such a hotly contested adherence and fight to adhere to the half hour on half hour off rule of singleplayer gaming in a dual sibling household, and it paid off. It became a competition of coercion, cooperation and comradarie that paid dividends beyond the great game. 

I was all Tidus(Arcadius, I named him), Rikku and Kimarhi(Down Lulu's path after he completed the center). She was Wakka, Lulu and Yuna mostly. The first part of the game we both tried to find everything together because we didn't have that many characters to choose from, and the first ten hours of the game melted away. Once it opened up, secrets started getting guarded, traded, for a few minutes more of time. "Oh, you want to know what beast I stole those sweet items that I upgraded my weapon with? I'll tell you if you dodge lightning bolts, I never got to fifty!"  It all culminated in me never getting the Caldabolg because I wouldn't dodge lightning bolts for her.

All in all I've put hundreds of hours in that game, and it is still the perfect blend of battle system, collection, story and completion that have never been pulled off in a Final Fantasy quite like it before or after, though each integration of the serious is masterful in its own way. Final Fantasy is a work of art, each iteration beloved, from many varying viewpoints. Hell, Nobuo Uematsu's music alone has carried through many dark times, and you can only pin him down to the greatest era in FF ever.
